labs.title: Grant least-privilege Azure RBAC access
labs.summary: Use Access control (IAM) to check access, remove an over-privileged assignment, add Reader at resource group scope, and verify effective access.
labs.scenario: Alex from Finance needs to read resources in **rg-finance-reports**. During the access check you find Alex already has **Contributor** at the subscription, which is broader than the request. Remove the over-privileged assignment, add **Reader** at the **resource group** scope, and use **Check access** to prove Alex can view but not change resources.
learningObjectives: Explain how a role assignment combines a security principal, a role and a scope
Choose between Reader, Contributor and Owner using the principle of least privilege
Recognize that assignments at a resource group apply to every resource inside it
prerequisites: Lesson: Azure RBAC, Zero Trust, and Microsoft Defender for Cloud

sources.title: Assign Azure roles using the Azure portal
What is Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC)?

components.text: Welcome to the **simulated** Contoso Cloud Portal. Everything on these pages is fictional and runs only in your browser.
Select a resource group to open it.
Resource group for the finance reporting storage account and dashboard.
This resource group hosts the marketing website. It is not part of Alex's request.
Role assignments at this scope apply to every resource in **rg-finance-reports**. Inherited subscription roles are broader.

options.label: Contributor - Manage resources, but not access

checks.message: Use resource group scope, not subscription scope.

steps.title: Open Access control (IAM)
steps.instruction: Go to **Resource groups**, open **rg-finance-reports**, and select **Access control (IAM)**.
steps.explanation: Azure RBAC assignments are evaluated at scopes such as subscription, resource group, or resource.

steps.title: Check Alex’s current access
steps.instruction: Select **Check access**, choose **Alex - Finance analyst**, and select **Check access**.
steps.hint: Inherited access may come from a broader scope.
steps.explanation: Check access shows effective permissions after inheritance, so it reveals broad assignments before you add a narrower one.

rules.description: Inherited Contributor was found during Check access

steps.title: Remove the over-privileged assignment
steps.instruction: Return to **Access control (IAM)** and remove Alex’s inherited **Contributor** assignment.
steps.explanation: Contributor can change resources. Removing subscription-scope Contributor prevents write access across unrelated resource groups.

steps.title: Add the least-privileged role assignment
steps.instruction: Select **Add role assignment**. Choose **Reader**, **Resource group: rg-finance-reports**, member **Alex - Finance analyst**, **Condition** **None**, then **Review + assign** and **Assign**.
steps.hint: Reader at resource group scope is enough for viewing reports.
steps.explanation: A role assignment combines role, member, and scope. Least privilege grants only what the task requires.

steps.title: Verify with Check access
steps.instruction: Use **Check access** again for Alex and confirm **Reader on rg-finance-reports** with **Can modify resources** **False**.
steps.hint: The result should not say Contributor or Owner.
steps.explanation: Verification proves Alex can complete the read-only task without retaining write permissions.

steps.title: Review final assignments
steps.instruction: Return to **Access control (IAM)** and confirm Alex has only **Reader** at **rg-finance-reports**.
steps.hint: No Contributor or Owner assignment should remain for Alex.
steps.explanation: A final review catches accidental extra access before you finish the access request.

finalRules.description: Alex has Reader and no write-capable role
No access was granted to Priya

labs.solution:
1. Open **Resource groups** > **rg-finance-reports** > **Access control (IAM)**.
2. Select **Check access**, choose **Alex - Finance analyst**, and note inherited **Contributor**.
3. Remove Alex’s **Contributor** assignment.
4. Select **Add role assignment**. Choose **Reader**, **Resource group: rg-finance-reports**, **Alex - Finance analyst**, **None**, then **Review + assign** and **Assign**.
5. Run **Check access** for Alex again and confirm Reader with no modify permission.

tr.title: Simüle bir portalda en az ayrıcalıkla erişim verin
tr.summary: Bir finans analistine doğru kapsamda salt okunur erişim vermek için Azure rol tabanlı erişim denetimi kavramlarını kullanın.
tr.scenario: **Contoso** şirketinde finans analisti olan Alex'in **rg-finance-reports** kaynak grubundaki raporları görüntülemesi gerekiyor. Alex kaynakları **değiştirememeli veya silememeli**. Göreviniz, **simüle** bir portal kullanarak doğru kapsamda en az ayrıcalıklı yerleşik rolü atamak. Tüm kişiler ve kaynaklar kurgusaldır.

open-resource-group.title: Finans kaynak grubunu açın
open-resource-group.instruction: **Resource groups** sayfasına gidin ve **rg-finance-reports** grubunu açın.
open-resource-group.hint: Sol gezinmeyi veya ana sayfadaki hızlı bağlantıları kullanın.
open-resource-group.explanation: Kaynak grubu, erişim yönetimi için geçerli bir **kapsamdır**. Burada yapılan rol ataması gruptaki tüm kaynaklara uygulanır.

open-iam.title: Erişim denetimini (IAM) açın
open-iam.instruction: Kaynak grubu için **Access control (IAM)** düğmesini seçin.
open-iam.explanation: IAM sayfası bu kapsamdaki **rol atamalarını** gösterir. Her atama bir güvenlik sorumlusunu (kim), bir rol tanımını (ne) ve bir kapsamı (nerede) birleştirir.

assign-reader.title: Alex'e en az ayrıcalıklı rolü atayın
assign-reader.instruction: **Alex**'in kaynakları görüntülemesini ancak değiştirmemesini sağlayan bir rol ataması ekleyin.
assign-reader.hint: Alex'in yalnızca görüntülemesi gerekiyor. Hangi yerleşik rol okumaya izin verir ama yazmaya izin vermez?
assign-reader.explanation: **Reader** rolü kaynakları görüntülemeye izin verir ancak değiştirmeye izin vermez. Contributor ve Owner, gerekenden fazla erişim vererek **en az ayrıcalık ilkesini** ihlal eder.

labs.title: Create and tag a resource group with a simulated Azure CLI
labs.summary: Practise beginner Azure CLI commands in a safe sandbox: explore, create a tagged resource group and add a zone-redundant storage account.
labs.scenario: **Tailwind Traders** is starting a small learning project. Using the **simulated** command line, create a resource group named **rg-learn-dev** in **West Europe**, tag it with **env=dev** and **owner=training**, and add a zone-redundant storage account named **stlearndev001**. Do not delete the existing shared resource group. Nothing you type is executed on real infrastructure.
learningObjectives: Use the Azure CLI command structure: az <group> <subgroup> <command> --parameters
Create a resource group in a region and apply tags for organization and cost tracking
Choose a storage redundancy option (SKU) that matches a requirement
prerequisites: Lesson: Azure portal, Cloud Shell, CLI, PowerShell, and Azure Arc
Lesson: Storage accounts, redundancy, and access tiers

sources.title: az storage account - Azure CLI reference

config.welcome: Simulated Azure CLI sandbox. Type 'help' to list the available commands. Nothing runs on real Azure resources.

steps.title: See what already exists
steps.instruction:
List the existing resource groups as a table:

`az group list --output table`
steps.hint: Type the command exactly as shown and press Enter.
steps.explanation: `az group list` returns the resource groups in the current subscription. `--output table` formats the result for people instead of scripts.

steps.title: Find the region name
steps.instruction:
Show the available regions and find the name for **West Europe**:

`az account list-locations --output table`
steps.hint: The CLI uses short names such as westeurope for regions.
steps.explanation: Commands use the region **name** (for example `westeurope`). The display name is only for people.

steps.title: Create the resource group
steps.instruction: Create **rg-learn-dev** in **West Europe**.
steps.explanation: A resource group is a logical container for resources that share a lifecycle. Its location stores the group's metadata.

rules.failureFeedback: rg-learn-dev was not found in westeurope yet.

steps.title: Tag the resource group
steps.instruction: Make sure **rg-learn-dev** has the tags **env=dev** and **owner=training**.
steps.hint: Either add --tags env=dev owner=training when you create the group, or run: az group update --name rg-learn-dev --tags env=dev owner=training
steps.explanation: Tags are name/value pairs. They help you organize resources and group costs, for example by environment or owner.

rules.description: rg-learn-dev has the env and owner tags

steps.title: Add a zone-redundant storage account
steps.instruction: Create the storage account **stlearndev001** in **rg-learn-dev** using **zone-redundant storage** (ZRS).
steps.hint: az storage account create --name stlearndev001 --resource-group rg-learn-dev --sku Standard_ZRS
steps.explanation: The SKU sets the redundancy. **Standard_ZRS** copies data across availability zones in one region, so the data stays available if one zone has a problem.

rules.description: stlearndev001 exists in rg-learn-dev with ZRS
rules.failureFeedback: Check the name, resource group and SKU (Standard_ZRS).

steps.title: Verify your work
steps.instruction:
List what you created, for example:

`az resource list --resource-group rg-learn-dev --output table`
steps.hint: az storage account list --resource-group rg-learn-dev --output table also works.
steps.explanation: Verifying after a change is a good habit - scripts and people both make typos.

rules.description: You listed the resources you created

finalRules.description: The shared production resource group still exists
finalRules.successFeedback: You left the shared production resources untouched.
finalRules.failureFeedback: rg-shared-services was deleted. Deleting a resource group deletes everything in it - reset the lab and try again.

labs.solution:
```
az group list --output table
az account list-locations --output table
az group create --name rg-learn-dev --location westeurope --tags env=dev owner=training
az storage account create --name stlearndev001 --resource-group rg-learn-dev --sku Standard_ZRS
az resource list --resource-group rg-learn-dev --output table
```

**Why:** the resource group groups the project's resources; the tags identify the environment and owner for organization and cost reporting; `Standard_ZRS` keeps copies across availability zones in the region.

tr.title: Simüle Azure CLI ile kaynak grubu oluşturun ve etiketleyin
tr.summary: Güvenli bir sanal ortamda temel Azure CLI komutlarını deneyin: keşfedin, etiketli bir kaynak grubu oluşturun ve bölge yedekli bir depolama hesabı ekleyin.
tr.scenario: **Tailwind Traders** küçük bir öğrenme projesine başlıyor. **Simüle** komut satırını kullanarak **West Europe** bölgesinde **rg-learn-dev** adlı bir kaynak grubu oluşturun, **env=dev** ve **owner=training** etiketlerini ekleyin ve **stlearndev001** adlı bölge yedekli (ZRS) bir depolama hesabı ekleyin. Mevcut paylaşılan kaynak grubunu silmeyin. Yazdığınız hiçbir şey gerçek altyapıda çalıştırılmaz.

explore.title: Mevcut kaynakları görün
explore.instruction:
Mevcut kaynak gruplarını tablo olarak listeleyin:

`az group list --output table`
explore.hint: Komutu gösterildiği gibi yazıp Enter tuşuna basın.
explore.explanation: `az group list`, geçerli abonelikteki kaynak gruplarını döndürür. `--output table` sonucu insanlar için biçimlendirir.

find-region.title: Bölge adını bulun
find-region.instruction:
Kullanılabilir bölgeleri gösterin ve **West Europe** için adı bulun:

`az account list-locations --output table`
find-region.hint: CLI, bölgeler için westeurope gibi kısa adlar kullanır.
find-region.explanation: Komutlarda bölge **adı** (örneğin `westeurope`) kullanılır. Görünen ad yalnızca insanlar içindir.

create-group.title: Kaynak grubunu oluşturun
create-group.explanation: Kaynak grubu, aynı yaşam döngüsünü paylaşan kaynaklar için mantıksal bir kapsayıcıdır.

tag-group.title: Kaynak grubunu etiketleyin
tag-group.instruction: **rg-learn-dev** grubunun **env=dev** ve **owner=training** etiketlerine sahip olduğundan emin olun.
tag-group.hint: Oluştururken --tags env=dev owner=training ekleyin veya az group update --name rg-learn-dev --tags env=dev owner=training komutunu çalıştırın.
tag-group.explanation: Etiketler ad/değer çiftleridir; kaynakları düzenlemeye ve maliyetleri gruplamaya yardımcı olur.

create-storage.title: Bölge yedekli bir depolama hesabı ekleyin
create-storage.instruction: **rg-learn-dev** içinde **bölge yedekli depolama** (ZRS) kullanan **stlearndev001** hesabını oluşturun.
create-storage.hint: az storage account create --name stlearndev001 --resource-group rg-learn-dev --sku Standard_ZRS
create-storage.explanation: SKU yedekliliği belirler. **Standard_ZRS**, verileri bir bölgedeki kullanılabilirlik alanlarına kopyalar.

verify.title: Çalışmanızı doğrulayın
verify.instruction:
Oluşturduklarınızı listeleyin, örneğin:

`az resource list --resource-group rg-learn-dev --output table`
verify.hint: az storage account list --resource-group rg-learn-dev --output table da çalışır.
verify.explanation: Değişiklikten sonra doğrulama yapmak iyi bir alışkanlıktır.

labs.title: Design an order portal architecture
labs.summary: Select Azure services for hosting, data, identity, monitoring and governance, and connect the web tier to its database.
labs.scenario:
**Adventure Works** wants an online order portal.

- The web front end should need **minimal server management**.
- Orders require a **relational database** with transactions.
- Product images are stored as **files**.
- Staff sign in with their **company accounts**.
- The operations team must **monitor performance** and **enforce** that resources are deployed only to approved regions.

Place the most suitable service cards in each zone and connect the web tier to the order database.
learningObjectives: Match business requirements to IaaS, PaaS and serverless compute options
Choose between relational, non-relational and object storage
Identify identity, monitoring and governance services
prerequisites: Lesson: Virtual machines, containers, and Azure Functions
Lesson: Storage accounts, redundancy, and access tiers

zones.label: Application hosting
zones.description: Where the web front end runs

zones.label: Data
zones.description: Where orders and images are stored

zones.label: Monitoring and governance
zones.description: How the team observes and controls the environment

palette.label: Azure App Service
palette.description: Managed platform for web apps and APIs; the provider manages the OS and runtime patching.

palette.label: Azure Virtual Machines
palette.description: Full control of the operating system - and responsibility for managing it.

palette.label: Azure Functions
palette.description: Event-driven code that runs on demand.

palette.label: Azure Blob Storage
palette.description: Object storage for files such as images and documents.

palette.label: Azure Monitor
palette.description: Collects and analyzes metrics and logs.

palette.label: Azure Policy
palette.description: Evaluates and enforces rules, such as allowed locations.

steps.title: Choose the hosting service
steps.instruction: Place a compute service in **Application hosting** that minimizes server management.
steps.hint: Which option is a managed platform (PaaS) where you do not patch the operating system?
steps.explanation: **App Service** is PaaS: Microsoft manages the servers, OS and runtime patching, so the team focuses on the app. Virtual machines would add OS management work.

rules.description: App Service hosts the web front end
rules.failureFeedback: A managed web hosting platform fits 'minimal server management' best.

rules.description: No virtual machines in the hosting zone
rules.failureFeedback: Virtual machines require you to manage the operating system.

steps.title: Choose the data services
steps.instruction: Place services in **Data** for the orders (relational, transactional) and for the product images (files).
steps.hint: One card is a relational database; another is object storage for files.
steps.explanation: **Azure SQL Database** is a managed relational database that supports transactions. **Blob Storage** is optimized for unstructured objects such as images.

steps.title: Choose the identity service
steps.instruction: Place the service that lets staff sign in with company accounts in **Identity and access**.
steps.explanation: **Microsoft Entra ID** provides cloud identity, single sign-on and multifactor authentication for staff accounts.

steps.title: Choose monitoring and governance
steps.instruction: Place the services that **monitor performance** and **enforce approved regions** in **Monitoring and governance**.
steps.hint: One service collects telemetry; another evaluates rules such as allowed locations.
steps.explanation: **Azure Monitor** collects metrics and logs. **Azure Policy** can deny deployments to locations that are not allowed. Azure Advisor gives recommendations but does not enforce rules.

steps.title: Connect the web tier to the database
steps.instruction: Add a connection from **Azure App Service** to **Azure SQL Database**.
steps.explanation: The web app reads and writes orders in the database, so the two components are connected in the design.

rules.description: App Service is connected to Azure SQL Database

labs.solution:
- **Application hosting:** Azure App Service (PaaS - minimal server management).
- **Data:** Azure SQL Database for orders (relational, transactional) and Azure Blob Storage for product images.
- **Identity and access:** Microsoft Entra ID for staff sign-in.
- **Monitoring and governance:** Azure Monitor for performance and Azure Policy to enforce allowed regions.
- **Connection:** App Service -> Azure SQL Database.

Azure Functions, Cosmos DB and Azure Advisor are useful services, but they do not match these specific requirements as closely.

labs.title: Troubleshoot a blocked deployment
labs.summary: Read a fictional error log and settings, find why a deployment fails, and choose a fix that respects governance.
labs.scenario: A developer at **Northwind Traders** reports that deploying a storage account fails immediately, while the same template works for a colleague. Investigate the fictional environment below and resolve the issue without weakening governance.
learningObjectives: Recognize when Azure Policy denies a deployment
Choose diagnostic steps: error details and policy assignments at inherited scopes
Select a fix that complies with governance requirements
prerequisites: Lesson: Azure Policy and resource locks

sources.title: Lock your resources to protect your infrastructure

context.environment: Northwind Traders assigned an **Allowed locations** policy to the management group that contains all production subscriptions. Production data must stay in the EU.
symptoms: A developer's storage account deployment to **East US** fails immediately.
The same template deployed to **West Europe** succeeds for a colleague.
context.logs:
Deployment failed (simulated log)
Status: Failed
Error: The resource was disallowed by policy.
Policy assignment: 'Allowed locations - production'
Requested location: eastus
constraints: Production data must remain in EU regions.
Governance policies may only be changed through the change-approval process.

stages.prompt: What is the most likely cause of the failure?

options.text: Azure Policy denies the deployment because East US is not an allowed location
options.feedback: Correct. The error names the policy assignment, and the requested location is not in the allowed list.

options.text: The Contributor role cannot create storage accounts
options.feedback: Contributor can create and manage resources; it only cannot manage access. The error also points to a policy, not permissions.

options.text: A CanNotDelete lock blocks new deployments
options.feedback: A CanNotDelete lock prevents deletion of the locked resources, and here it is on a different resource group.

options.text: The storage account name is already taken
options.feedback: A name conflict produces a different error, and the same template works in West Europe.

stages.prompt: Which diagnostic steps help confirm the cause? Select all that apply.

options.text: Read the error details in the deployment history or activity log
options.feedback: The error details identify the policy assignment and requested location.

options.text: Review policy assignments inherited from the management group and subscription
options.feedback: Policies assigned at a higher scope are inherited by subscriptions and resource groups below it.
This is destructive and would not remove a policy inherited from the management group.
The failure happens in the cloud control plane, not on the local computer.

options.text: Redeploy the storage account to West Europe or North Europe
options.feedback: This meets the data residency requirement and complies with the policy.

options.text: Remove the policy assignment so any region can be used
options.feedback: This weakens governance and breaks the EU data residency requirement.

options.text: Give the developer the Owner role to bypass the policy
options.feedback: A Deny policy applies regardless of the deployer's role.

options.text: Add a resource lock to the subscription
options.feedback: Locks prevent changes or deletion; they do not allow a denied location.

stages.prompt: Explain your reasoning in one or two sentences.
stages.modelAnswer: The error shows that the 'Allowed locations' policy assigned at the management group denied the request for East US. Policies are inherited by every subscription below the management group, so deploying to an allowed EU region fixes the issue while keeping the data residency requirement.

steps.title: Identify the likely issue
steps.instruction: Read the symptoms, log and settings, then choose the most likely cause.
steps.hint: Look closely at the error message in the log.
steps.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates requests to Azure Resource Manager. With the **Deny** effect, non-compliant requests are rejected before any resource is created.

steps.title: Choose diagnostic steps
steps.instruction: Select the steps that confirm the cause.
steps.hint: Where are deployment errors recorded, and where can policies be assigned?
steps.explanation: Error details and the list of policy assignments at every inherited scope tell you exactly which rule blocked the request.

steps.title: Select a solution
steps.instruction: Choose the fix that resolves the issue without weakening governance.
steps.explanation: The compliant fix is to deploy to an allowed region. Changing the policy would require the approval process and would break the data residency rule.

steps.title: Explain your reasoning
steps.instruction: Write a short explanation of what happened and why your fix works.
steps.explanation: Explaining your reasoning helps you remember the pattern for next time.

labs.solution:
**Walkthrough**

1. The log says the resource was **disallowed by policy** and names the **Allowed locations - production** assignment.
2. The assignment is at the **management group** scope, so it is inherited by every production subscription and resource group.
3. The request used **eastus**, which is not in the allowed list (westeurope, northeurope). The **Deny** effect blocks the request.
4. Roles do not bypass Deny policies, and the CanNotDelete lock is unrelated.
5. **Fix:** deploy to West Europe or North Europe. If the business truly needs another region, request a policy change or exemption through the approval process.
